svg.title: Scene 60: A qubit, and the rule that turns amplitudes into odds
svg.desc: Four frames. 1, a qubit state alpha times ket 0 plus beta times ket 1, with alpha squared plus beta squared equal to 1; for alpha 0.866 and beta 0.5 the signed amplitude bars and the probability bars, 0.75 and 0.25. 2, a second state with amplitudes plus 0.707 and minus 0.707: the minus sign shows in the amplitude bar but the probabilities are 0.50 and 0.50. 3, a hundred identically prepared copies of the first state each measured once: every result is a definite 0 or 1, and 75 of the hundred read 0. 4, a fair coin and the plus state both give 50:50 when measured directly, but after a Hadamard gate the plus state always reads 0 while the coin is still 50:50, so classical randomness is not the same as superposition.
svg.text: A qubit, and the rule that turns amplitudes into odds
Two amplitudes describe a qubit; their squares are the odds of reading 0 or 1.

g.text: 100 copies of state 1, each measured once
each result is one definite bit
A coin is not a superposition
Measured directly, a fair coin and |+⟩ both give 50 : 50.
Apply H first: |+⟩ reads 0 every time; the coin stays 50 : 50.
Randomness from not knowing is not the same as
Purple: amplitudes (minus shown in pink). Teal: probabilities = |amplitude|².
